questions.question: When driving on snow or ice:

options.text: It is safe to use cruise control.
Change your speed and direction slowly and gradually.
Drive the same way you would on dry roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your speed and direction slowly and gradually.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, make all speed and direction changes slowly. Do not use cruise control on snow or ice. Your tires may lose grip, and you could lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop and look both ways before going.
Let other traffic go first before you enter or cross.
Keep steady speed and watch for traffic from all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other traffic go first before you enter or cross.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and be ready to stop. Let any car, bike, or person pass before you go. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must always stop at railroad crossings, like school buses and trucks with hazardous materials.
Watch for multiple trains.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Watch for vehicles that must stop at crossings, such as school buses and hazardous material trucks.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: You can eliminate them with one mirror on each side.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than regular cars. Other drivers should avoid these areas.

questions.question: If you drive slower than other traffic, you will most likely:

options.text: Block traffic and get a ticket.
Help traffic move better.
Show good defensive driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block traffic and get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Drive slower only when there is heavy traffic or bad weather. If you drive too slowly and block normal traffic, you may get a ticket. Match the speed of traffic unless it exceeds the legal speed limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The right road has one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right for road work.
The road ahead turns sharply at a steep angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply at a steep angle.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn about conditions right ahead. This sign tells you to slow down for a sharp turn in the road.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely when:

options.text: All vehicles are going about the same speed.
One lane is going faster than other lanes.
One vehicle is going faster or slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle is going faster or slower than other traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen more often when one driver goes faster or slower than other cars on the road. Speeding increases crash risk. Driving slower also creates danger because cars behind you may hit you or swerve to avoid you.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate traffic lanes:

options.text: Passing is allowed from the left.
Passing is allowed from the right.
Passing is not allowed from either side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either side.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: Tired driving increases the risk of:

options.text: Missing your exit.
Being late.
Falling asleep and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes mistakes with speed and distance. It slows your decisions and increases crash risk. When tired, you may fall asleep at the wheel and crash, hurting or killing yourself or others.

questions.question: When you see flashing red lights at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than the train.
Come to a complete stop.
Find a way around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing signs warn about trains ahead. You must obey all railroad signs and lights. Never try to drive around barriers.

questions.question: A driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Pass the vehicle slowly at 10 mph or less.
Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes and pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. You cannot see if pedestrians are crossing. Stop and only move when all pedestrians have crossed.

questions.question: If you drive faster than other vehicles on a two-lane road and keep passing cars, what will happen?

options.text: You will reach your destination faster and safer.
You will increase your chance of a crash.
You will help reduce traffic congestion.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will increase your chance of a crash.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing other vehicles on two-lane roads. Each time you pass, your risk of a crash increases.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body and reduces its effects.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.
Watch for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Watch for another train after the first one passes. Do not move until all gates are raised and all warning lights stop flashing.

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use light braking.
Brake hard and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use light braking.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, take your foot off the accelerator and slow down gradually. Do not use the brakes until the vehicle has slowed significantly.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads:

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
You can see better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip on loose gravel and dirt than on concrete or asphalt. Slow down on these roads. It takes longer to stop and it is easier to skid when turning.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness and concentration.
Reaction time and coordination.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your nervous system. It reduces alertness and concentration, slows reaction time, and reduces coordination.

questions.question: Which statement is true about large trucks?

options.text: They take longer to stop than passenger cars.
All trucks have air brakes that allow quick stops.
They are easier to steer than passenger cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than passenger cars.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than cars at the same speed. A car at 55 mph stops in about 400 feet. A truck at 55 mph needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: Which of these blocks smooth traffic flow?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes causes traffic congestion and should be avoided.

questions.question: When you see a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is completely clear of your path.
Honk your horn as you pass them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is completely clear of your path.
questions.explanation: When you see a person using a white cane or guide dog, stop until they are well away from your vehicle. Always give blind pedestrians the right of way.

questions.question: You must use low beams when you are:

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water droplets and create glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you automatically have the right-of-way. Always check the situation at an intersection. Yield your right-of-way if it helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: If you become tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop to rest or change drivers.
Drink coffee.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or change drivers.
questions.explanation: Stop to rest or change drivers if you feel tired. Tiredness slows your thinking and reactions, making driving unsafe.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no one can cross the center to pass, no matter which direction they are going.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving means anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off driving. It is the most common cause of car crashes. Distractions cause you to miss important sights and sounds needed to avoid crashes.

questions.question: After passing another vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane when you:

options.text: Cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
Have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before moving back to your lane, make sure you are far enough ahead of the other vehicle. When you see both of its headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to return to your lane safely.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn.
Get ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the protected green arrow is ending. Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic pass before you turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
School zone.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a crosswalk. Watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
Traffic signal ahead.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down to avoid crashes and brake damage.
